evidence.description: The revision checked out in the fixture repository while reviewing.

findings.claim: The README now says ./check.sh --selftest validates every contributor change and that a pass means a change to tally.py is correct. The check runs four fixed word-count cases only, so a wrong change passes it.

evidence.description: Replaced the body of lines() in tally.py with return 0, so --lines is wrong for every input. The required check still passes; tally.py --lines on a two-line file prints 0.
evidence.command: sed -i 's/return len(text.splitlines())/return 0/' tally.py && ./check.sh --selftest && printf 'a\nb\n' > in.txt && python3 tally.py --lines in.txt

evidence.description: check.sh runs four fixed word-count cases and none with --lines.

findings.proposedRemedy: Restore the baseline's description: the check runs its built-in cases and checks those only. Separately, add cases for --lines.

findings.claim: The new --lines option has no case in check.sh, so a regression in it is not caught.

evidence.description: check.sh runs four fixed word-count cases and none with --lines.

findings.proposedRemedy: Add --lines cases to check.sh, including an empty file and a file without a trailing newline.

limitations: Did not review tally.py's handling of non-UTF-8 input; out of the stated scope.
